title: Lifting one constant finite matrix to discrete point matrices
statement: Let X,Y be schemes in universe u, f:Y→X, A a commutative ring in universe u and k a commutative ring in universe u+1. Fix e:ULift A≃+*k and any ring-sheaf isomorphism c:underline k≅smallRing(X,p_X^*discreteObj A), using [def-sfb-integral-models-stacks-data]. Let N be an internal p_X^*discreteObj A-module and U an object of the coefficient-sized pro-etale site of Y [def-sfb-affine-locally-constructible-proetale-modules]. Put F=f^*(coefficientModelFixedScalars(smallModules(N) restricted along c)), and write u_V:V→Y for the scheme map of a site object. Fix natural numbers m,n and a k-linear map q:k^m→k^n. If F on the slice at U is isomorphic to the constant sheaf of coker q [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], there is a covering sieve S on U such that for every g:V→U in S there exists a map d:(discreteObj A)^m→(discreteObj A)^n of regular point modules with (u_V≫f)^*N≅p_V^*coker d [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]. No Noetherian hypothesis on k or any scheme is imposed. No locally constant predicate or scheme covering family is assembled here. The returned point matrix has precisely the specified ranks m and n. The notation for the actual finite free module, inverse-image module and point pullback is fixed in [def-sfb-point-model-free-module], [def-sfb-point-model-restriction-module], [def-sfb-point-model-pullback-functor]; these are the existing constructions, not additional hypotheses.

source.place: Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules; Sites Tag 00YV, proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi. Reverse finite-matrix part of lem-sfb-discrete-coefficient-local-models, steps 1--2.

proof.text: Apply constant_slice_internal_presentation to the given slice trivialization. This produces an internal free matrix a of the specified ranks on the underlying scheme of U and an isomorphism from its cokernel to the internal restriction of N.

Apply discrete_internal_matrix_local_lifting to a. It supplies a covering sieve and, on each member, a point matrix d and an arrow isomorphism between the pulled-back matrix a and the point pullback of d.

Inverse images preserve finite colimits: for scheme pullback this is the existing instance; for point pullback lift the monoidal point inverse-image left adjunction to modules. Thus both preserve cokernels. Apply cokernel.mapIso to the arrow isomorphism. Compose these cokernel comparisons with the pullback of the internal presentation isomorphism. The site-morphism triangle g≫U.hom=V.hom and upperStarComp identify the source with pointModelRestriction at V. This gives the desired point cokernel with the unchanged ranks m,n.

lean.statement:
theorem discrete_constant_presentation_lifting
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X)
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (k : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing k]
    (e : ULift.{u + 1} A ≃+* k)
    (c : ConstantCompletion.constant (Scheme.coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, u} X) k ≅
      smallRing X (condensedRingObj (discreteObj A) X))
    (N : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1})
      (condensedRingObj (discreteObj A) X))
    (U : Scheme.coefficientProEtaleSiteModel.{u, u} Y)
    (m n : ℕ)
    (q : ModuleCat.of k (Fin m → k) ⟶ ModuleCat.of k (Fin n → k))
    (hN : Nonempty (((Scheme.coefficientProEtaleFixedModulePullback.{u, u} f k).obj
          ((coefficientModelFixedScalars _ k).obj
            ((smallModules X (condensedRingObj (discreteObj A) X) ⋙
              ConstantCompletion.res c.hom).obj N))).over U ≅
      (constantSheaf ((Scheme.coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, u} Y).over U)
        (ModuleCat.{u + 1} k)).obj (cokernel q))) :
    ∃ S : Sieve U, S ∈ Scheme.coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, u} Y U ∧
      ∀ (V : Scheme.coefficientProEtaleSiteModel.{u, u} Y) (g : V ⟶ U), S g →
        ∃ d : pointModelFree (discreteObj A) m ⟶ pointModelFree (discreteObj A) n,
          Nonempty
            (pointModelRestriction (discreteObj A) f N (AsSmall.down.obj V).hom ≅
              (pointModelPullbackFunctor (discreteObj A) (AsSmall.down.obj V).left).obj
                (cokernel d))
